validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE CONFIRMED independent of GEM/wiki via a corporate lineage traceable through federal and state filings: Alabama-Tennessee Natural Gas Company (in service by 1950 per Huntsville Utilities' own history, hsvutil.org/about_hu/history.php: 'The City of Huntsville purchased the gas system and contracted with the Alabama-Tennessee National Gas Company to pipe natural gas into Huntsville' in 1950) -> Enbridge Pipelines (AlaTenn) Inc./L.L.C. (FERC Docket CP02-429-000, Federal Register 2002-09-06, operating under a pre-existing 'blanket certificate issued in Docket No. CP85-359-000') -> transferred to American Midstream, LLC effective 2009-11-01/closed 2009-11-04 (Alabama PSC filing, pscpublicaccess.alabama.gov, Wilkerson & Bryan P.C. letter dated 2009-12-15) -> American Midstream (AlaTenn), LLC (FERC Docket CP19-476-000, Federal Register 2019-06-18, Decatur Compression Station upgrade) -> BBT AlaTenn, LLC, a Black Bear Transmission LLC subsidiary (FERC Docket CP24-524-000, Federal Register 2024-10-15, 'AlaTenn Pride Loop Project') -> present. CLASSIFICATION CONFIRMED: FERC-regulated interstate natural gas transmission pipeline under the Natural Gas Act across all four dockets found, consistent with PHMSA's own safety-brochure classification (pipelinesafetyinfo.com, 'BBT AlaTenn, LLC', DOT Guide# 115 'Natural Gas') and BBT's own site description ('FERC-Regulated Interstate' transmission, blackbearllc.com/natural-gas-transmission). NO DUPLICATE against the 45-pipeline US-gas roster: P0236 Ozark Gas Transmission shares the same immediate former owner (Black Bear Transmission LLC) but is a physically distinct Arkansas/Missouri-area system -- see the cross_row_leads note on the ownership-change finding that also applies there. OWNERSHIP HAS CHANGED SINCE THE ROW WAS WRITTEN, as flagged in the task brief: Enstor Pipeline Holdings, LLC closed its acquisition of Black Bear Transmission Opco, LLC from Basalt Infrastructure Partners on 2025-11-12 (pgjonline.com 2025-11 'Enstor Completes Acquisition of Black Bear Transmission, Adding 1,700 Miles of Pipelines'; enstorinc.com/news/enstor-completes-purchase-black-bear-transmission; blackbearllc.com/natural-gas-transmission itself now banners 'Black Bear is now owned by Enstor Gas') -- see the dedicated attribution concern below for the corrected Owner1 fill.

validity.recommendation: correct StartYear1 from 2002 to approximately 1950 -- 2002 is the filing year of a minor delivery-point extension under an existing decades-old blanket certificate, not an in-service date
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's StartYear1=2002 does not hold up. The only 2002 event found is FERC Docket CP02-429-000 (Federal Register, 2002-09-06): Enbridge Pipelines (AlaTenn) Inc. requesting authority for a small new delivery point in Madison County, AL to serve one end-user (Metal Working Products), explicitly 'under AlaTenn's blanket certificate issued in Docket No. CP85-359-000' and referencing a second blanket certificate 'issued in Docket No. CP89-2201-000' -- i.e. the system was already operating under FERC blanket authority at least 13-17 years before 2002, so 2002 is very likely a data-entry conflation of this filing's year with the pipeline's actual in-service date. Huntsville Utilities' own institutional history (hsvutil.org/about_hu/history.php, independently fetched and confirmed) states directly: '1950 -- The City of Huntsville purchased the gas system and contracted with the Alabama-Tennessee National Gas Company to pipe natural gas into Huntsville,' naming the same company (Alabama-Tennessee Natural Gas Co., AlaTenn's original name) as the gas supplier via this same pipeline corridor. A related 1963 Alabama Supreme Court case, Alabama-Tennessee Nat. Gas Co. v. City of Huntsville (found via law.justia.com and courtlistener.com), could not be independently read (both blocked the fetch with HTTP 403) -- flagging this as a single-direct-source finding (hsvutil.org) for the specific year, corroborated only circumstantially (not to an exact year) by the two pre-1990 FERC blanket certificates. Tier medium given that limitation.

validity.recommendation: flag LengthKnown=475 km / 294 mi as stale, not wrong as originally researched -- current operator disclosure states 325 miles (~523 km), and a 2024 FERC filing supplies the likely cause
validity.researcher_notes: Two things are both true here. (1) The sheet's recorded 475 km (~295 mi) is corroborated within rounding by Rextag's independent pipeline database (rextag.com/pages/bbt-alatenn: 'Miles of Pipeline: 294' / 'a 294-mile pipeline running from Selmer, Tennessee to Huntsville, Alabama'; 294 mi = 473.2 km, a 0.4% delta from the sheet's 475 km) -- see the Length [ref] fill below, staged as REFS_ADDED at the ORIGINAL value per the rounding-agreement rule. (2) BBT's own current operator page (blackbearllc.com/natural-gas-transmission) now states '325 miles' for AlaTenn -- about 31 miles (50 km) more than Rextag's figure. FERC Docket CP24-524-000 (Federal Register, 2024-10-15, 'AlaTenn Pride Loop Project,' filed 2024-09-24, i.e. AFTER this row's LastUpdated of 2023-08-24) explains the gap: BBT AlaTenn acquired a '37-mile-long pipeline (Trigas Line)' and built connecting piping in Colbert County, Alabama -- 294 + 37 = 331 mi, closely matching BBT's current 325-mi figure. Recommend updating LengthKnown to reflect the post-acquisition total (BBT's own 325 mi / ~523 km) the next time this row is revisited, citing CP24-524 for the acquisition and blackbearllc.com for the current aggregate -- not doing so now only because BBT's page does not itself cite a source and a second fully-independent current-mileage figure was not found.

validity.recommendation: flag Capacity=200 MMcf/d as likely understated -- BBT's own current disclosure states 292 MDth/d (290 MDth/d under firm-transportation contracts)

contested.CapacityUnits: MDth/d (source's own unit; ~MMcf/d, not an exact 1:1 conversion)

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Capacity=200 MMcf/d is not confirmed by any source found; BBT's own current operator page (blackbearllc.com/natural-gas-transmission) instead states '292 MDth/d capacity, 290 MDth/d FT contracts.' A dekatherm (Dth) is a heat-content unit (1 Dth = 1 MMBtu) commonly treated as approximately equal to 1 Mcf of pipeline-quality gas, but the two are not identical, so 292 MDth/d is not a precise substitute for an MMcf/d figure -- flagging as a spec concern rather than a clean like-for-like correction. Two FERC dockets independently confirm capacity has grown since the row's 2023-08-24 LastUpdated and since whenever 200 MMcf/d was originally set: CP19-476-000 (2019, Decatur Compression Station -- abandoning four compressors totaling 1,455 hp and installing two new ones totaling 3,550 hp, a net increase, cost $5,415,200, 'to provide additional firm transportation service to the City of Huntsville... and improve system reliability') and CP24-524-000 (2024, 'AlaTenn Pride Loop Project' -- new pipe plus the acquired 37-mile Trigas Line, 'to provide its customers with enhanced gas supply access and increased operational flexibility'). No single source states a directly comparable MMcf/d total, so the corrected value is staged as a caveat here rather than a clean fills[] overwrite -- see the Capacity [ref] fill below for the single-source REFS_ADDED disposition.

validity.recommendation: correct EndState/Province from the multi-value 'Mississippi, Alabama' to a single terminus, 'Alabama' -- Mississippi is a pass-through state, not an endpoint (batch rule: one terminus per row)
validity.researcher_notes: Per the task brief's own flag, EndState/Province='Mississippi, Alabama' is the known multi-value defect. Two independent sources resolve it cleanly: Rextag (rextag.com/pages/bbt-alatenn) states the pipeline runs 'from Selmer, Tennessee to Huntsville, Alabama' and separately notes it 'extends through northeast Mississippi and northern Alabama' -- Mississippi is explicitly described as a pass-through corridor, not a terminus. PHMSA's Alabama-specific safety brochure for this exact operator (pipelinesafetyinfo.com/user/file/Alabama/BBT%20AlaTenn%20LLC.pdf) lists 'COUNTIES OF OPERATION: Colbert, Madison, Lawrence, Morgan, Limestone' -- all Alabama, with Madison County containing Huntsville, the stated terminus. (Note: a separate combined PHMSA Mississippi brochure exists covering 'BBT AlaTenn LLC / BBT MIDLA LLC / BBT Mississippi LLC' together and lists Mississippi counties, but it covers three legal entities jointly and does not establish that AlaTenn itself terminates in any of them -- consistent with Rextag's pass-through description rather than contradicting it.) See the Location [ref] fill below for the full corrected value set (also adding StartLocation=Selmer, TN and EndLocation=Huntsville, AL, both currently blank on the sheet).

validity.recommendation: update Owner1 from 'Black Bear Transmission LLC' to 'Enstor Pipeline Holdings, LLC' (100%), dated to the 2025-11-12 closing -- ownership changed after this row was researched
validity.researcher_notes: As flagged in the task brief, ownership of the whole Black Bear Transmission cluster (including P0236 Ozark, see cross_row_leads) changed after this row was last researched. Enstor Pipeline Holdings, LLC (subsidiary of Enstor Gas) announced a purchase agreement 2025-08-19/20 for Black Bear Transmission Opco, LLC from funds advised by Basalt Infrastructure Partners (worldpipelines.com, 2025-08-20; enstorinc.com/news/enstor-acquire-black-bear-transmission-basalt-infrastructure-partners) and CLOSED the acquisition 2025-11-12 (pgjonline.com, 'Enstor Completes Acquisition of Black Bear Transmission, Adding 1,700 Miles of Pipelines'; enstorinc.com/news/enstor-completes-purchase-black-bear-transmission, stating Black Bear comprises 'nine regulated transmission systems totaling approximately 1,700 miles... approximately 2.6 Bcf/d'). Independently, BBT's own current site (blackbearllc.com/natural-gas-transmission) now banners 'Black Bear is now owned by Enstor Gas.' Three independent sources (buyer's own release, trade press, seller-branded operating site) triangulate on the same fact and date -- tier high. Note the acquired entity's legal name carries an 'Opco' suffix ('Black Bear Transmission Opco, LLC') not present in the sheet's current Owner1 string ('Black Bear Transmission LLC') -- flagging this naming precision alongside the ownership change rather than asserting they are proven identical without a corporate-structure chart. This does not disturb Operator=BBT AlaTenn LLC (the operating subsidiary name is unaffected by the parent-level ownership change) or PipelineType/Status.

summary: P0185 AlaTenn Gas Pipeline (Selmer, TN -> Huntsville, AL, legacy system in service since ~1950) is confirmed real, correctly classified (gas transmission), and not a duplicate of P0236 Ozark; staged REFS_ADDED on all 11 MISSING_REF units (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Capacity, Length, Diameter, Location, Operator, Owner, plus Pressure and Start which needed corrected values) with 3 genuinely UNRESOLVED MISSING_VALUE units (Proposal, Construction, FuelSource -- all explained by the system's pre-FERC-e-filing vintage or its multi-receipt-point structure) and 1 UNRESOLVED-owed cost (SegmentCost, legacy system predates any discoverable original build cost). Six validity concerns staged: StartYear1 corrected 2002->1950 (medium), Length flagged stale (475km/294mi confirmed as-researched but BBT's current site + a 2024 FERC Trigas-Line acquisition point to ~325mi/523km now, medium), Capacity flagged stale (200 MMcf/d vs BBT's current 292 MDth/d, medium), the task-flagged EndState/Province multi-value defect corrected 'Mississippi, Alabama'->'Alabama' (high), and an attribution concern updating Owner1 'Black Bear Transmission LLC'->'Enstor Pipeline Holdings, LLC' following Enstor's 2025-11-12 acquisition close (high) -- the same ownership change flagged for P0236 via cross_row_leads. Status confirmed operating (evidence through 2025-11), no status change proposed.
